questions.questionText: (a) Calculate 24 × 6. (b) State whether the answer is a factor of 288. (c) Give one factor other than 1 and the number itself.
questions.explanation: (a) 24×6=144. (b) Yes, because 144×2=288. (c) Any proper factor such as 6 is acceptable.

questions.questionText: Given x=3, y=4, z=5, calculate xy+z² and then 2x+3y−z.
Solve the equation 4x + 7 = 35. Show the algebraic steps and check your answer.
questions.explanation: Subtract 7 from both sides to get 4x=28; divide by 4, giving x=7. Substitution gives 4(7)+7=35.

questions.questionText: A rectangular garden is 11 m long and 8 m wide. Find (a) its perimeter, (b) its area, and (c) the cost of fencing it at $3 per metre.
questions.explanation: Perimeter=2(11+8)=38 m. Area=11×8=88 m². Fencing cost=38×$3=$114.

questions.questionText: A triangle has angles 39° and 54°. Calculate the third angle. If the triangle is isosceles, state a possible condition on its other angles.
questions.explanation: Third angle=180−39−54=87°. For an isosceles triangle, two angles must be equal; this condition depends on the given values.

questions.questionText: Using π=22/7, calculate the circumference and area of a circle of radius 9 cm.
A right-angled triangle has legs 3 cm and 10 cm. Calculate the hypotenuse, giving your answer to 1 decimal place.
In a right-angled triangle, opposite side to θ is 3 cm and adjacent side is 11 cm. Calculate tan θ and use a calculator to find θ to 1 decimal place.
The data set is 11, 4, 7, 10, 13. Calculate the mean and median.
questions.explanation: Mean=45/5=9. After ordering the five values, the middle value is 10.

questions.questionText: A box contains 6 red, 6 blue and 2 green counters. One counter is selected at random. Find P(red) and P(not blue).
An arithmetic sequence has first term 5 and common difference 7. Find (a) the nth term, (b) the 10th term, and (c) the sum of the first 10 terms.
Given f(x)=x²−2x+5, calculate f(6) and solve f(x)=5 for real x.
For matrix A = [[4, 3], [9, 5]], find det(A). State whether A has an inverse.
questions.explanation: det(A)=ad−bc=4×5−3×9=-7. A 2×2 matrix is invertible exactly when its determinant is non-zero.

questions.questionText: Find the gradient and equation of the line through (2,8) and (7,11).
Simplify (a) (x+4)² and (b) (x−7)(x+7).

In ΔABC, AB = 8.5 cm, BC = 11.2 cm, and ∠ABC = 62°.
(a) Use the Cosine Rule to calculate AC correct to 3 significant figures. [3 marks]
(b) Calculate the area of ΔABC correct to 3 significant figures. [2 marks]
Solve the quadratic equation 3x² - 5x - 4 = 0, giving your answers correct to 2 decimal places. [4 marks]

A bag contains 5 red balls and 3 blue balls. Two balls are drawn at random WITHOUT replacement.
(a) Find the probability that both balls are red. [2 marks]
(b) Find the probability that the two balls are of different colours. [3 marks]

In a geometric progression, the 2nd term is 12 and the 5th term is 324.
(a) Find the common ratio r and first term a. [3 marks]
(b) Calculate the sum of the first 6 terms. [2 marks]

A cylindrical water tank of internal radius 1.4 m and height 3.0 m has a hemispherical dome removed? No — a solid metal cone of radius 6 cm and perpendicular height 8 cm is melted and recast into small spheres of radius 1 cm.
(a) Calculate the volume of the cone in terms of π. [2 marks]
(b) How many complete spheres of radius 1 cm can be made? [3 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) V_cone = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π(36)(8) = 96π cm³ [2 marks].
(b) V_sphere = (4/3)π(1)³ = (4/3)π cm³ [1 mark]. Number = 96π ÷ (4π/3) = 96 × 3 / 4 = 72 spheres [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
Points A(1, 2), B(3, 2), and C(3, 5) form ΔABC. Matrix M = [[0, -1], [1, 0]] maps ΔABC onto ΔA₁B₁C₁.
(a) Calculate the coordinates of A₁, B₁, and C₁. [3 marks]
(b) Describe fully the single geometric transformation represented by M. [2 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) M·(1,2) = (-2, 1) = A₁; M·(3,2) = (-2, 3) = B₁; M·(3,5) = (-5, 3) = C₁ [3 marks].
(b) Rotation through 90° anticlockwise about the origin (0, 0) [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
Given O is the origin, OA = a, OB = b, point M is the midpoint of AB, and point P lies on OB such that OP : PB = 2 : 1.
Express in terms of a and b:
(a) AB [1 mark]
(b) OM [2 marks]
(c) MP [2 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) AB = AO + OB = b - a [1 mark].
(b) OM = OA + ½AB = a + ½(b - a) = ½a + ½b [2 marks].
(c) OP = (2/3)b, so MP = MO + OP = -½a - ½b + (2/3)b = -½a + (1/6)b [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
The cost C of producing n textbooks consists of a fixed cost k plus a variable cost proportional to n (C = k + mn). When 100 books are printed, C = $700; when 250 books are printed, C = $1,450.
(a) Find k and m. [3 marks]
(b) Calculate the cost of printing 400 textbooks. [2 marks]

A ship sails 18 km from port P on a bearing of 040° to Q, and then 24 km due East from Q to R.
(a) Show that ∠PQR = 130°. [1 mark]
(b) Calculate distance PR correct to 1 decimal place. [3 marks]
(c) Calculate the bearing of R from P to the nearest degree. [3 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) North line at Q gives alternate interior 40° south-of-Q-to-P? Wait: North at P makes 040° with PQ, so interior angle between South at Q and QP is 40°; angle between South and East is 90°, hence ∠PQR = 40° + 90° = 130° [1 mark].
(b) PR² = 18² + 24² - 2(18)(24)cos 130° = 324 + 576 - 864(-0.6428) = 900 + 555.37 = 1455.37 -> PR = 38.1 km [3 marks].
(c) sin(∠QPR)/24 = sin 130°/38.15 -> sin(∠QPR) = 0.4819 -> ∠QPR = 28.8°. Bearing = 040° + 29° = 069° [3 marks].

questions.questionText: Solve the inequality system and list the integer values of x satisfying: 2x - 1 > 5 and x + 3 ≤ 10. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: 2x - 1 > 5 -> 2x > 6 -> x > 3 [1.5 marks]. x + 3 ≤ 10 -> x ≤ 7 [1.5 marks]. Integers satisfying 3 < x ≤ 7: {4, 5, 6, 7} [1 mark].
